entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The 7 July 2005 London bombings were a pivotal event in modern British history, marking a turning point in the country's response to terrorism. On 7 July 2005, four British Muslim men affiliated with al-Qaeda in the Islamic Maghreb detonated explosives on four London public transportation systems, killing 52 people and injuring over 700 others. 

The bombings targeted the Piccadilly line, resulting in mass casualties and widespread destruction. This devastating event led to increased security measures and changes in British society and politics. 

In the aftermath of the bombings, the British government implemented various counter-terrorism policies, including the introduction of the Terrorism Act 2006. The event also led to a significant increase in Islamophobia and anti-Muslim sentiment in the UK. 

The 7 July 2005 London bombings serve as a poignant reminder of the devastating consequences of terrorism and the importance of addressing the root causes of extremism. 'We will not be cowed by terrorism' — Prime Minister Tony Blair's statement in the aftermath of the bombings encapsulates the resilience of the British people in the face of such atrocities.
